evidence.note: Recognized the lane-immediate-packed-in-MemArg.offset representation was 'hacky' and considered a cleaner dedicated Instr variant, but chose to barrel ahead with the messy hack rather than rework the foundation — the anti-pattern for this dimension (later forced special-case lane validation on top of it).

After noticing assert_invalid failures dominate (1375 of them) and that per-test patching couldn't reach 1.0, stepped back and added an entirely new validate.rs type-checker — a structural response to the root generator of failures, flipping many downstream assertions.

When the new validator regressed SIMD tests (dropped to 31%, rejecting valid modules), correctly diagnosed that the validator skipped SIMD ops and added SIMD validation rather than reverting or patching individual tests.

When SIMD shift families stubbornly failed, traced root cause to a miscategorized opcode range (107-109 wrongly in the binary v128,v128 list) in the shared validate_simd_other helper and chose to completely rewrite the categorization function once, rather than patch each family — fixing the generator of failures.
Recognized the trunc bounds were semantically wrong (rejecting valid -2147483648.9) and corrected the underlying bound formula rather than special-casing the failing test.
Mostly local safety patches for panics (bounds-checked indexing, memory limit checks, trap-message tweaks) — legitimate but surface-level fixes rather than structural rethinks.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly hit the 8-anchor behavior: it recognized when a failure signaled a structural problem — adding a whole validator module when assert_invalid dominated, and rewriting the miscategorized shared validate_simd_other helper once so many families flipped together — rather than piling per-instance patches. However, it is pulled below a clean 8 by a notable counterexample: it consciously identified the lane-in-offset value representation as messy yet chose to barrel ahead rather than rework it, and much of the mid-game was surface patching. The reactive (not proactive) nature and the un-reworked hacky representation keep it short of 8-10, so a 7 best captures the interpolation between 'reconsiders when a family fails' and 'refactors the shared cause once.'
